title: Neuromuscular Blockade — Reversal & Monitoring
sources: Critical Vector — Anesthesia Reference: TOF Depth Classification + Reversal Dosing + NMB Duration (ASA 2023)
ASA 2023 Practice Guidelines for Monitoring and Antagonism of Neuromuscular Blockade

changelog.change: Initial entry — TOF-depth-based reversal choice and dosing, the NMB duration table, factors prolonging block, and the ASA 2023 quantitative-monitoring standard.

summary: Confirm a TOF ratio ≥ 0.9 on a QUANTITATIVE monitor before extubation — visual / tactile assessment cannot detect residual fade above a TOF count of 4. Sugammadex reverses aminosteroids (rocuronium, vecuronium) at any depth; neostigmine only works from a shallow / minimal block and never on a deep one.

rows: Sugammadex 4 mg/kg IV (roc/vec). Neostigmine CANNOT reverse a deep block. After roc 1.2 mg/kg RSI needing immediate reversal: sugammadex 16 mg/kg
Sugammadex 2 mg/kg IV (roc/vec). Neostigmine NOT recommended at this depth
Sugammadex 2 mg/kg (recommended). Neostigmine 15–40 mcg/kg is an acceptable alternative ONLY with quantitative confirmation that TOF ≥ 0.4 first
Sugammadex 2 mg/kg (preferred), OR neostigmine 15–40 mcg/kg + glycopyrrolate 0.01 mg/kg
No pharmacologic reversal needed — safe to extubate

body.text: Cisatracurium and atracurium (benzylisoquinoliniums): sugammadex does NOT reverse them — use neostigmine 40–70 mcg/kg + glycopyrrolate (they also undergo Hofmann elimination). Sugammadex has no effect on succinylcholine either. Giving neostigmine when the patient is already fully recovered (TOF ≥ 0.9) can cause paradoxical weakness — don't reverse a block that isn't there.

rows: ~3 min after roc 1.2 mg/kg — a CICO 'wake the patient' option
10–15+ min. ALWAYS pair with glycopyrrolate 0.01 mg/kg (ratio ~ 0.2 mg glyco : 1 mg neo) or atropine 0.02 mg/kg

Encapsulates aminosteroids only. Re-curarisation is rare but monitor ≥ 30 min. Renal failure → the complex accumulates (still generally preferred over cis + neostigmine, per 2024 data). Can bind hormonal contraceptives — advise a backup method for 7 days

body.text: Prolongs the block: hypothermia, hypermagnesaemia (obstetrics!), acidosis, aminoglycoside antibiotics, volatile anaesthetics (potentiate), hepatic failure (aminosteroids), renal failure (vecuronium, pancuronium), and pseudocholinesterase deficiency (succinylcholine → phase-II / prolonged apnoea → support ventilation until spontaneous recovery; sugammadex does not help).

ASA 2023 monitoring standard: use a QUANTITATIVE monitor (acceleromyography or EMG) at the adductor pollicis (ulnar nerve); calibrate before induction; confirm TOF ratio ≥ 0.9 before extubation. Qualitative visual / tactile assessment of fade is unreliable above a TOF count of 4 and is NOT an acceptable sole extubation criterion.
